subject: Request: LLM interaction logging policy, retention timeline & SCC mapping
messages:

Subject: LLM interaction logging: retention windows, pseudonymization, and SCC mapping

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for taking this. We're running a privacy review ahead of our vendor selection and need a concise artifact that answers the following for Redwood's hosted inference product:

1) What fields of an application-LLM interaction are logged server-side (full prompt text, user identifiers, metadata like IP/region, model invoked, returned tokens)?
2) How long are each of those items retained in raw or derived form (e.g., full prompt: 30 days; tokenized cache: 7 days)?
3) Is any textual data used to train models (please confirm: "no-train" by default or opt-in only)?
4) Pseudonymization/aggregation: what techniques are applied before longer-term storage?
5) Please attach any SOC 2 scope summary, SCC mapping matrix, and a diagram of the dataflow for inference requests.

We need something we can attach to our DPA/Security review and map back to our internal controls. If possible, can you provide this by Tue, 2028-09-12?

Jordan
Director, Vendor Risk
BankCo Financial Services

From: rafael_mendes@redwoodai.com

Cc: neha_kapoor@redwoodai.com, marissa_cole@redwoodai.com
Date: Fri, 07 Sep 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LLM interaction logging: retention windows, pseudonymization, and SCC mapping

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Neha and Marissa from Security & Privacy to provide the formal artifacts. High level answers inline; Neha will follow up with the formal matrix and diagrams.

1) Logged fields (hosted API, default config):
   - request_timestamp, model_id/version, route_id
   - request_metadata: client_ip (anonymized to /24 in EU), region, user_agent
   - payload: full prompt text and any appended tool-call parameters (retained by default but configurable)
   - response: generated tokens (full response) and top-n logits/metadata (if enabled for diagnostics)
   - billing/usage counters and token counts

2) Default retention windows (hosted):
   - Full prompts & responses: 30 days (default)
   - Tokenized caches/KV (ephemeral caches for serving): up to 72 hours; not persisted across major upgrades
   - Audit logs (non-text metadata): 1 year (rotated/archived)
   - Aggregated usage metrics: 24 months (P-aggregated, no PII)

3) Training on customer data: Redwood's hosted offering is "no-train" by default. Customer data is not used to update model weights unless a customer opts into a separate training program and signs a scoped agreement.

4) Pseudonymization & minimization:
   - We support prompt redaction hooks at ingestion (customer-configurable), automatic token hashing for identifiable fields (configurable regex), and default IP truncation for EU requests.
   - Longer-term storage uses truncated hashes + KMS-wrapped salts for strength where required by contract.

5) Attached (preliminary): SOC 2 summary, high-level dataflow diagram, and a draft SCC mapping matrix. Neha will send the formal SCC mapping spreadsheet and a short cover note addressing the DPA clauses.

Next steps: Neha — can you confirm and produce the formal artifacts (SCC matrix + exportable dataflow) and a one-page statement we can hand to legal?

Thanks — Rafael
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

(attachments referenced: redwood-soc2-summary-2028.pdf, llm-dataflow-diagram.drawio)

Subject: Re: LLM interaction logging: retention windows, pseudonymization, and SCC mapping

Hi Jordan — thanks, attaching the formal artifacts and an executive note below. I've also included a mapping to the SCC clauses you asked about.

Executive statement (short):
Redwood Inference's hosted inference endpoint does not use customer prompt/response data to train or improve our public model weights unless a customer explicitly opts into a separate, contractual training program. By default, plaintext prompts and generated responses are retained for 30 days to support abuse detection, quality investigation, and billing reconciliation. Customers can enable a "no-retain" profile in which all textual payloads are redacted at ingestion and only non-text metadata is logged for up to 7 days for operational troubleshooting.

Technical artifacts attached:
 - SCC mapping: scc-mapping-matrix.xlsx (columns: SCC control, DPA clause, Redwood control description, evidence pointers)
 - Dataflow diagram: llm-dataflow-diagram.drawio (includes KMS boundaries, VPC overlay, and path for ephemeral caches)
 - SOC 2 summary: redwood-soc2-summary-2028.pdf (scope: infra + platform controls for hosted inference; note: SOC 2 report available under NDA)

Key technical notes:
 - Pseudonymization: we apply configurable hashing for PII patterns (regex-based), and support customer-supplied salt keys via KMS for stronger unlinkability.
 - Long-term storage of any textual content is only performed under explicit retention policies in customer contract or regulatory requirement; otherwise content is purged by the 30-day workflow.
 - For EU customers exercising GDPR rights, we provide an export-and-delete workflow; deletion events are reversible only via documented retention policies (e.g., legal hold).
 - HIPAA: Redwood offers a HIPAA addendum for covered entities; under that profile we can route inference traffic through a dedicated private deployment and limit retention per the agreement.

Evidence pointers: Please find details (tabbed) in the SCC matrix and the drive link below. Per your request, the SOC 2 full report will be shared via our secure transfer once the NDA is in place.

Attachments: scc-mapping-matrix.xlsx, llm-dataflow-diagram.drawio, redwood-soc2-summary-2028.pdf

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
